The reported fiber electrodes mostly use oxides, transition metal sulfide or Prussian blue analogues as the cathode materials, which are highly compatible with fiber forming process. The discharge platform voltage of these substances is low, often below 2.5 V, and their mechanical properties decay rapidly with the charge-discharge cycle. The anode materials are usually choosing sodium metal, graphene or carbon fiber. Metal sodium is easy to form metal dendrites to puncture the separator and cause short circuit of the energy storage device. If the battery is damaged, the metal sodium is easy to directly harm the skin of the wearer. The great challenge for graphene or carbon materials anodes are the irreversible capacity loss of the first cycle is too large. For fiber lithium-ion batteries /sodium-ion batteries, the electrolyte uses flammable organic electrolyte. This further increases the risk of fiber batteries. Exploring reliable energy storage devices with high energy density and power density are indeed the key component that affects the application of renewable devices . Recent years, enormous endeavors devoted to rechargeable fiber-shape batteries because of their long cycle life, little self-discharge rate, high energy density and large application potential . Among these, rechargeable sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are emerged as one of the most promising choices for significantly low cost of sodium sources as well as similar working principle with commercial lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) .

Fiber electrodes play a pivotal role in the electrochemical performance of flexibility and energy storage for fiber batteries . Therefore, the exploitation of appropriate fiber electrodes with a suitable structure is highly desirable to the further commercialization of fiber batteries . According to the previous reports, several fiber-shape SIBs have been developed. For example, Jiupeng Zhaoet al . directly employed 2 D tungstate and graphene oxide (GO) nanosheets to construct fiber electrodes via wet-spinning technique. The fiber-shaped SIBs exhibited the reversible capacities of 178 mA h g-1 . Teng Zhaiet al . embedded yolk-shell NiS2 nanoparticles into porous carbon fibers. as-prepared fiber SIBs achieved a high reversible capacity of about 679 mA h g-1 at 0.1 C . Guiyin Xuet al . the fiber-shape electrodes were successfully prepared by wet spinning following freeze-dried, which were fabricated with porous GO, carbon nanotube and tin oxide. The assembled SIBs demonstrated a reversible capacity of 164.1 mA h g-1 at 0.5 A g-1 . However, most of the full fiber-shaped electrodes in SIBs were directly used sodium metal fiber as anodes, and the operating voltage plateaus of the SIBs were lower than 1.5 V. These would result in energy density and power density below desired levels .

As lithium-ion battery manufacturing technology develops, the application variety of capacity and cathode material is increasing significantly. First, to reduce the complexity of battery formation, the capacity tends to be larger ; secondly, due to the difficult compatibility of energy density and safety characteristics, various cathode material-based batteries are adopted in different application scenarios, e.g., LFP and NCM batteries . Specifically, in pursuing long cycle life and low cost, such as ESS with ultra-large installed capacity and automotive power-oriented pioneering LIBs manufacturers, LFP batteries have a more significant advantage ; the NCM batteries with high energy density are widely used in EVs with extremely high range requirements. Besides, NCM batteries are divided into three types, i.e., low-nickel-content (e.g., Li(Ni1/3Co1/3Mn1/3)O2(NCM333)), medium-nickel-content (e.g., Li(Ni0.5Co0.2Mn0.3)O2(NCM523)) and high-nickel-content (e.g., Li(Ni0.6Co0.2Mn0.2)O2(NCM622) and NCM811) . Medium-nickel content battery is an optimized solution after balancing thermal stability and energy density. However, product terminals equipped with the above-all battery types have been subject to safety accidents and even explosions [ ], causing great public concern and hindering the acceptance of LIBs. In addition to the relatively large number of EV safety incidents, MWh-class ESS has not been spared. In particular, the ESS explosion that occurred in April 2021 in Dahongmen, Beijing, China, caused several casualties . The battery installed in this 25 MWh ESS is the LFP battery, which is generally known to be safe from previous studies [ ]. However, it is seen that the hazard level of this accidental catastrophe is equally enormous and unbearable compared with NCM battery-related disasters. Therefore, conducting a safety performance assessment study on lithium-ion batteries widely deployed in the current multi-application scenarios is urgent and essential.

With the increasing large-scale application of clean and sustainable energy, the demand for energy storage devices has grown rapidly over the past years. At the moment, certain batteries are dominating the markets of portable electronics, electric vehicles, and grid-scale energy storage systems. However, the scarce resources and safety issues limit their further applications. Therefore, an alternative should be considered, which leads to the resurgence of interest in aqueous batteries with the advantages of high performance and low cost for large-scale application. Various oxides were first reported as promising cathode materials. However, the poor structural stability of these materials, resulting from dissolution and structure collapse during cycling, restricts their practical applications.

In contrast, other oxides also attract abundant attention owing to the merits of multiple valences, rich crystal structure, and high theoretical performance. Among them, layered oxides are considered as promising cathode candidates because the open frameworks provide numerous diffusion paths and storage space for ions. However, the long-term performance of layered oxides is unsatisfactory owing to the stability penalty induced by the aqueous system and large ion radius. To overcome these issues, tremendous efforts have been devoted over the past few years. Among them, interlayer engineering is an effective strategy to stabilize the layered frameworks. Various metal ions have been pre-introduced into layered oxides to enlarge the interlayer spacing and strengthen the structural stability. Another common strategy is defect engineering, which could induce the electronic structure reconfiguration and accelerate charge transfer kinetics to boost the reversible ion storage. For instance, anionic vacancies have been induced to reduce the strong electrostatic interaction between oxides and ions, reducing lattice strain due to ion insertion/extraction and accelerating ion transport. Meanwhile, several reports have proposed the introduction of cationic vacancies to provide additional sites for ion storage to improve the performance. However, only cationic or anionic defects have limit effects on enhancing the electrochemical performance. Therefore, coupling interlayer and defect engineering may offer a reliable opportunity to construct high performance and stable layered oxide cathodes for batteries.
